label: rem:descent-reduction-zero
title: Reduction at dimension 0
html:
When \dim M_k = 0, the base manifold is a discrete set of points, and the geometric data of the archimedean quantum observable universe reduce to purely algebraic invariants at each point p\in M_k.

  1. Connection. The \mathrm{SU}(2) connection A_k lacks directions for parallel transport. Its curvature F_A vanishes identically and the holonomy is trivial.
  2. Bundle. The principal \mathrm{SU}(2) bundle \mathcal{S} restricts to its fibre \mathcal{S}_p over the point p. The fibre and the group action completely determine the bundle.
  3. Substrate parameter. The substrate parameter q(p) = 1 + \lVert L\wedge F_A^{+}\rVert(p) (\mathbb{C}-substrate via Levi form) assigns a definite quantum constant q\in[1,\infty) to each point, encoding the full QOU content at that point.
  4. Reeb direction. The absence of a tangent space removes the Reeb vector field (q-Reeb vector field) and the horizontal distribution. Only the internal \mathrm{SU}(2) fibre data persist.

In this terminal stage, the fibre \mathcal{S}_p and the value q(p) determine every observable. When M_k consists of several points, the descent data decompose into independent summands, one per point. When M_k is a single point, the pair (\mathcal{S}_p, q(p)) captures the entire QOU.
